<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Direct Target-Agent SFT</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the sequential adaptation experiment, we directly fine-tune the
Qwen3.5-9B target agent on successful no-intervention trajectories from the
same task-level training split used to construct the engineer data. We retain
one trajectory for each benchmark and canonical task identity, yielding 2,515
complete multi-turn episodes: 901 from WebShop, 774 from ALFWorld, and 840
from DBBench. The optimization settings not listed below, including the
optimizer, learning rate, schedule, warmup, precision, and seed, are identical
to the cold-start SFT configuration above.</p>
</div>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Executable Patch Interface</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A patch can intervene at four positions in the target agent’s execution
lifecycle. Each hook receives benchmark-specific runtime context and returns
only an effect defined by the host runtime.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table C.1: </span>Executable lifecycle hooks.</figcaption>
<table id="A3.T1.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A3.T1.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A3.T1.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">
<span id="A3.T1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">
<span id="A3.T1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Hook</span></span>
</span></th>
<th id="A3.T1.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">
<span id="A3.T1.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Invocation and effect</span></span>
</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A3.T1.5.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T1.5.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A3.T1.5.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">
<span id="A3.T1.5.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">on_init</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T1.5.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">
<span id="A3.T1.5.2.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Before the first target decision; adds reusable task guidance or a tool hint.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T1.5.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T1.5.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">
<span id="A3.T1.5.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">make_pre_hint</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T1.5.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">
<span id="A3.T1.5.3.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.3.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Before a target decision; injects a state-conditioned message without
executing an action.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T1.5.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T1.5.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">
<span id="A3.T1.5.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">on_before_action</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T1.5.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">
<span id="A3.T1.5.4.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.4.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.4.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">After the target proposes an action but before environment execution; may
block and reprompt or, where supported, rewrite or force the pending action.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T1.5.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T1.5.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A3.T1.5.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">
<span id="A3.T1.5.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">on_post_step</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T1.5.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A3.T1.5.5.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A3.T1.5.5.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T1.5.5.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">After environment feedback; injects recovery guidance or, where supported,
schedules a next action.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The return contract separates contextual guidance from action mediation.
<span id="A3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">make_pre_hint</span> returns a <span id="A3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">message</span>, and
<span id="A3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">on_post_step</span> may return an <span id="A3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inject_hint</span> effect.
<span id="A3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">block_and_prompt</span> suppresses the current pending action and asks the
frozen target to choose again. Where enabled, <span id="A3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">rewrite_action</span>
replaces that pending action, while <span id="A3.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">force_action</span> selects a concrete
action for the current or next execution step. DBBench v1 accepts soft
guidance and blocking but does not execute SQL rewrites or forced commits.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The engineer generates the patch before the rerun and does not participate in
the subsequent task interaction. It never calls an environment tool or
submits a final task answer directly; the host runtime alone interprets the
hook’s structured effects. Candidates that do not yield an installable
intervention, are behaviorally inert, or do not complete evaluation are
treated as no intervention and receive zero reward. A valid, complete patch
instead receives its full-batch performance difference, including a negative
value when it causes regressions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Data Construction and Task Splits</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We split benchmark tasks before collecting trajectories or generating harness
patches. The SFT and online-RL training sets contain the task identities used
to construct their respective training signals. The validation set is used
only for checkpoint selection, and the test set is used only for final
evaluation. Table <a href="#A4.T1" title="Table D.1 ‣ Appendix D Data Construction and Task Splits ‣ Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a> reports numbers of distinct benchmark
tasks, rather than numbers of trajectories, failure packets, generated
patches, or optimizer samples.</p>
</div>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">WebShop.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use task indices 0–499 as the fixed test set. A separate training pool is
randomly divided at the task-batch level into SFT and RL partitions with seed
20260603. We then reserve 100 tasks from the RL partition for validation with
seed 20260623; the remaining 5,190 tasks form the RL training set. WebShop
task generation uses goal seed 233 throughout baseline and patched execution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ALFWorld.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We stratify by the six ALFWorld task families. The 500-task test set contains
all 109 tasks from the official <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">new_std</span> split and a stratified
391-task sample from <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">train_valid</span>. With seed 20260614, the remaining
tasks are divided into 1,380 SFT tasks and an RL-side partition; 99 RL-side
tasks are reserved for validation, leaving 1,280 RL training tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DBBench.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We shuffle the 4,803 available training tasks with seed 20260625 and assign
2,401 tasks to SFT and 2,402 to the RL side. We reserve 100 RL-side tasks for
validation, leaving 2,302 RL training tasks. The separate 300-task standard
test set is used only for evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Teacher filtering, failure-packet construction, benchmark balancing, and
multi-candidate sampling operate within these task partitions. Their
resulting record counts are therefore training-accounting quantities, not
additional task splits.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para"><span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_ERROR undefined">\FloatBarrier</span>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Target-Agent Generalization</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We apply the single learned editing policy to a broad set of target agents that
are never used during training. For every target, the engineer reads that
target’s own failure traces and generates target-specific patches; this
measures transfer of the editing <em id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">policy</em>, not reuse of one fixed patch.
Table <a href="#A5.T1" title="Table E.1 ‣ Appendix E Target-Agent Generalization ‣ Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a> reports the per-target, per-benchmark task
success before and after installing the target-specific patches, providing the
absolute levels behind the delta heatmap in the main paper. WebShop uses the
fixed-seed 500-task rerun (goal seed 233); ALFWorld and DBBench use their
respective test sets. primary Qwen3.5-9B target that is also used in the main results.</p>

<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Every target-level average is positive, and across the full <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21\times 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21\times 3</annotation></semantics></math> matrix
<math id="A5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="56" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>56</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">56</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63</annotation></semantics></math> target–benchmark combinations improve, four are unchanged
(all on WebShop), and the three small regressions are WebShop on Llama-3.1-70B
(<math id="A5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.4</annotation></semantics></math>), ALFWorld on Qwen2.5-72B (<math id="A5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-2.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2.0</annotation></semantics></math>), and WebShop on Gemma-4-31B-it
(<math id="A5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.2</annotation></semantics></math>). The benchmark-averaged gain across the twenty unseen targets is
<math id="A5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.06</annotation></semantics></math> points, showing that a single training recipe transfers across model
families and scales without any per-target retuning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Held-Out Task Generalization</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further test whether patches inferred from a handful of failures improve
<em id="A6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unseen tasks</em>. For each benchmark and seed, every engineer observes the
same ten failures from the frozen Qwen3.5-9B target, generates one
benchmark-specific patch, and applies it to all remaining tasks; we repeat the
protocol over three matched evidence seeds. Invalid patches are counted as no
intervention (zero delta). Table <a href="#A6.T1" title="Table F.1 ‣ Appendix F Held-Out Task Generalization ‣ Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a> reports the pooled
held-out change (1,270 tasks) and, for reference, the full-split change
including the ten evidence tasks (1,300 tasks); the error term is the sample
standard deviation across the three seeds.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table F.1: </span>Held-out-task generalization from sparse failure evidence
(<math id="A6.T1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> success, pp; mean <math id="A6.T1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> sample std over three seeds). Valid counts
the seed-benchmark patches that installed a real intervention out of nine.</figcaption>

<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Harness-R1 improves pooled held-out success by <math id="A6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.9\pm 1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.9</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.9\pm 1.5</annotation></semantics></math> points and is
positive on every seed, whereas both frontier engineers average negative and
straddle zero across seeds. The larger frontier spreads (<math id="A6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 2.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 2.5</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 3.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>3.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 3.6</annotation></semantics></math>) reflect swings between marginal gains and sizable regressions, so
converting sparse failures into a broadly useful edit is a capability that scale
alone does not confer.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Lifecycle-Position Ablation</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To attribute the improvement to specific intervention points, we hold the frozen
vanilla target and the generated patches fixed and disable one lifecycle
position at a time, alongside a no-intervention control and the full patch.
Each configuration reruns the target three times per benchmark, and we report the
equal-benchmark-weighted success rate used in the main results.
Table <a href="#A7.T1" title="Table G.1 ‣ Appendix G Lifecycle-Position Ablation ‣ Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G.1</span></a> lists the per-benchmark and averaged success
behind the ablation figure in the main paper.</p>
</div>

(success rate, %). The <span id="A7.T1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Avg.</span> column is the equal-weight benchmark

<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The full patch reaches <math id="A7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="53.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>53.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">53.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> average success, <math id="A7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.9</annotation></semantics></math> points above no
intervention. Removing pre-action mediation or post-feedback recovery causes
the largest drops (<math id="A7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.9</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.3</annotation></semantics></math> points), while removing episode
initialization or pre-decision costs only <math id="A7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math> points. The
dominant position is environment-dependent: pre-action mediation matters most on
WebShop (success falls from <math id="A7.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="41.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>41.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">41.6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A7.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31.5</annotation></semantics></math>), whereas post-feedback
recovery matters most on ALFWorld (<math id="A7.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="52.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>52.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52.1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A7.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="41.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>41.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">41.9</annotation></semantics></math>). Because a single patch
can coordinate several positions, these effects are conditional and should not
be summed into a universal importance ranking.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p3" class="ltx_para"><span id="A7.p3.1" class="ltx_ERROR undefined">\FloatBarrier</span>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Qualitative Case Studies</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine three stored evaluations from the validation-selected Harness-R1
engineer used for the main frozen-target results. In every case, the target
agent is the same frozen Qwen3.5-9B model before and after patch installation,
and the patched run uses the same ten tasks as its baseline evidence. We
inspect the runtime trace in addition to the generated code, so that an
intended edit is not mistaken for an intervention that actually executed.
These cases illustrate distinct mechanisms and limitations; aggregate claims
are based on the full evaluations in the main paper rather than on the selected
examples.</p>
</div>

<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>WebShop: Correcting a Premature Purchase</h3>

<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Observed failure and generated edit.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In WebShop batch 008, several trajectories reached a relevant, in-budget
product but issued <span id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Buy Now</span> before choosing an option required by the
instruction. The engineer generated a single pre-action intervention. It
activates only for a normalized <span id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Buy Now</span> action and blocks the action
when either the current price exceeds the budget or a required product option
remains unselected. The resulting message asks the target to choose a visible
matching option, or return to search if no such option exists.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task-level behavior.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One task requests a synthetic hairpiece with a black-brown color and a price
below $40. The baseline target finds a suitable product but purchases it
without selecting the color, receiving a partial reward of 0.667. With the
patch installed, the target initially proposes the same premature purchase.
The guard blocks it, after which the target selects <span id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">black brown</span> and
then purchases the item, receiving reward 1.0.</p>
</div>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Across the ten-task batch, the same guard raises full successes from 2 to 5
and mean WebShop reward from 0.682 to 0.768, while preserving both tasks that
were already fully successful. This case shows that an effective harness edit
need not replace the target’s policy with a large controller: a low-bandwidth
intervention at the point of an unsafe action can preserve the target’s search
behavior while changing the final outcome.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>ALFWorld: Coordinating Multiple Lifecycle Positions</h3>

<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Observed failure and generated edit.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ALFWorld batch 045 contains recurrent failures in which the target finds an
object but omits a required transformation, moves toward the wrong receptacle,
or enters a transform–place loop. The generated patch coordinates four
positions in the execution lifecycle:</p>
</div>

<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Runtime behavior.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The intervention trace records 56 stage hints or guard messages across the
batch. For a task requiring a hot mug in a cabinet, the target successively
receives guidance to take the mug, heat it using the microwave, navigate to
the cabinet, and place the mug. For a task requiring a cooled egg on a
countertop, the target attempts to place the egg on a dining table; the
pre-action guard rejects that destination, and the subsequent trajectory
places the egg on the requested countertop.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">

<span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Take-target hint </span><math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> heat-at-microwave hint </span><math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
go-to-destination hint </span><math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> put-target hint</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Failure <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> success</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:72.5pt;">
<span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cooled egg on countertop</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Stage hint </span><math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> attempted wrong placement </span><math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
destination guard </span><math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> corrected placement</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Failure <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> success</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">At batch level, the patch rescues six baseline failures but regresses one
baseline success, producing a net change from 1/10 to 6/10. It also fails to
resolve every task: one two-object trajectory continues to alternate between
destination and placement guidance. The example therefore demonstrates a
genuine closed-loop harness policy, while also showing that stage tracking can
remain imperfect.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>A Failure Case of Direct Harness Editing</h3>

<div id="A8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An off-the-shelf model can access the complete lifecycle interface yet still
produce harmful interventions. On ALFWorld, Gemini-3.5-Flash receives full
failure evidence and may edit all four lifecycle positions. Its patches reduce
success from 208/500 (41.6%) to 177/500 (35.4%), a drop of 6.2 percentage
points. Among 39 valid patches, 21 reduce batch success, 12 improve it, and 6
leave it unchanged.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Overgeneralized action intervention.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The largest regression occurs in a batch whose success falls from 7/10 to
0/10. The patch installs broad <span id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">on_before_action</span> rules that force
actions from a locally plausible stage estimate. On two-object tasks, it
prematurely places the first object rather than collecting both objects before
placement, overriding decisions that the frozen target agent previously
executed correctly. This case illustrates why execution traces and a powerful
base model alone do not yield a reliable harness editor: a plausible diagnosis
can still compile into overly aggressive runtime behavior. Harness-R1 instead
post-trains the editing policy on realized task outcomes, directly penalizing
patches that degrade rerun performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.4 </span>DBBench: Preserving Schema and Stored-Value Conventions</h3>

<section id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Observed failure and generated edit.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DBBench batch 022 contains recurring failures around multi-word identifiers,
schema recovery, and exact mutation values. Harness-R1 generates a
stage-aware patch that recommends schema inspection after identifier errors,
asks the target to inspect the affected row before mutation, and verifies the
stored value before commit. The patch raises the frozen target from 4/10 to
6/10. On the same baseline evidence and tasks, a valid GLM-5.2 patch raises
the result only to 5/10.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task-level contrast.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One task asks the agent to change the length of the
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Moosehead Grand Prix</span> entry in the multi-word table
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Race Schedule</span>. The no-intervention trajectory recovers the quoted
table name and observes the existing value <span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">3 Hours</span>, but writes
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">4 hours</span>; the exact-format evaluator marks the task incorrect.
GLM-5.2 supplies general backtick and mutation-verification guidance, yet its
guided trajectory makes the same lower-case write. Harness-R1 first triggers
schema recovery, inspects the existing row, writes <span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">4 Hours</span> to match
the stored convention, and verifies the row before committing.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Runtime condition</span></span>
</span></th>
<th id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Batch success</span></th>
<th id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Example outcome</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">No intervention</span></span>
</span></th>
<td id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">4/10</span></td>
<td id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">4 hours<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif"> (failure)</span></span></td></tr>
<tr id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">GLM-5.2 patch</span></span>
</span></th>
<td id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">5/10</span></td>
<td id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">4 hours<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif"> (failure)</span></span></td></tr>
<tr id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Harness-R1 patch</span></span>
</span></th>
<td id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">6/10</span></td>
<td id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">4 Hours<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif"> (success)</span></span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This paired example does not rely on an invalid competitor output: both
engineers produce executable patches. The difference is that the
Harness-R1-guided run converts schema and row evidence into the exact stored
representation required by the task.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.5 </span>Cross-Case Interpretation</h3>

<section id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">WebShop.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The recurring failure is premature purchase. Harness-R1 installs a narrow
action guard conditioned on runtime predicates, although the guard cannot
repair an earlier choice of the wrong product.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ALFWorld.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The recurring failures are omitted transformations and incorrect placement.
Harness-R1 combines persistent stage state, targeted hints, and a placement
guard, while routing and two-object state can still cause regressions or
loops.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DBBench.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The recurring failures involve multi-word identifiers and exact mutation
formats. Harness-R1 uses schema recovery, row inspection, and
format-preserving verification; some value conventions still require
stronger neighborhood-level checks.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Together, the cases show that Harness-R1 learns environment-dependent editing
policies rather than one fixed prompt. Outcome-grounded post-training
increases useful executable edits without guaranteeing complete or
regression-free rules.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
